explanation: Pollution is any environmental change that adversely affects living organisms and represents the third main cause of species extinction. The notes highlight four major types of pollution that threaten biodiversity: 1) Acid deposition: sulfur and nitrogen emissions from vehicles form acid rain, which weakens trees and kills vital decomposers and small invertebrates in the soil. 2) Eutrophication: nutrient runoff causes massive algal blooms; when the algae die and decompose, it depletes the water's oxygen, killing aquatic life. 3) Ozone depletion: chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) degrade the atmosphere's protective ozone layer. 4) Synthetic organic chemicals: manufactured chemicals that can mimic hormones, disrupting wildlife development and reproduction.

questions.q: How does acid deposition from automobile emissions threaten terrestrial biodiversity?
opts: It directly destroys the ozone layer in the stratosphere.
It weakens trees and kills soil decomposers and small invertebrates.
It causes massive algal blooms in the epilimnion.
It blocks stomata, preventing water absorption.
